actual_scope: Characterize where the best integer quotient of the sharp net splitting tax N(t,sigma) switches as sigma varies: unique tie thresholds between adjacent quotients, their order and window, and the resulting staircase, for every 0<t<1.
scope_change_reason: The card asks about the five inherited framework assumptions. This package answers open next question 2 of CubeJerry's merged PR #6769 (research/sharp-net-splitting-tax), an analytic coefficient question, as a side result.
bottleneck_link: Side result: describes the structure of the compiler splitting coefficient N(t,sigma) used by the strictification test of #6769. It changes no native invoice, supplier or selected result, and discharges none of the five framework assumptions.

open_questions.question: Is theta_q = z(tau_q) - q below 1/2 for every 0<t<1 and every integer q>=1, and what is the constant c_t in 1/2 - theta_q ~ c_t/q?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would turn the window zeta(q+1) < tau_q < zeta(q) into a half-window and prove that rounding z to the nearest integer never overshoots the best quotient. The package certifies theta_q < 1/2 for 150 pairs only.
open_questions.first_step: Show g(z+1/2) > g(z-1/2) at fixed sigma, for example by proving the left slope of log g exceeds the right slope at equal distance from z, or by comparing F_{q+1} at the remainder s_q with g(q) at z = q + 1/2.
open_questions.blocked_by: No closed form for s_q or g; the comparison needs third-order information on the implicit maximizer.

open_questions.question: For the selected #6030 joint application of #6769, does the minimizing u of the strictification test (10) sit at a kink u = tau_m - t of N(t,t+u)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If P_x is a positive moment sum n_r r^x, the left side of (10) is convex in u with convex kinks (PROOF.md section 5, conditional remark). A solver that looks only for stationary points of one branch could then miss the optimum.
open_questions.first_step: Read the joint application linked from #6769, scan u over its exact directed moment intervals, and report whether the minimum lies at a threshold.
open_questions.blocked_by: The exact directed moments of that application, the moment form of P_x in #4433/#4480, and the complete outer consumer.

open_questions.question: Is tau_m(t) increasing in t for each fixed m?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The certified table suggests it, which would make the first switch point monotone in the exponent.
open_questions.first_step: Differentiate rho_m(sigma; t) = 1 implicitly in t, using the envelope formula for the sigma-slope.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs the t-derivative of the maximizing remainder s_q, which has no closed form.
